title: Learned ultrasound features classify breast sentinel-node involvement
summary: Image-pretrained convolutional models were fine-tuned on breast ultrasound images and combined with axillary ultrasound findings. In a retrospective second-hospital test of 395 women, the combined model classified pathology-referenced sentinel-node involvement with an AUC of 0.848. Avoided surgery was hypothetical, not an observed clinical benefit.
ai_technology: ImageNet-pretrained convolutional neural networks with ultrasound fine-tuning

evidence.tested: 937 patients from two hospitals: 542 for development and 395 for testing; 3,049 images. The reference was surgical lymph-node assessment. Radial and anti-radial image-model probabilities were fused.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective exclusions and ultrasound-visible lesion selection limit transfer. Images were processed individually without explicitly modeling their correlation. The separate sequential non-sentinel-node analysis has conditional denominators and is not represented by the quoted AUC. Supplementary architecture and threshold-selection details were not independently inspected; no reduced surgery or outcome benefit was measured.
evidence.ai_role: Convolutional networks pre-trained on 1.28 million ImageNet images learned ultrasound features through fine-tuning; their predicted probabilities enabled the node-involvement evaluation.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary clinical design, convolutional-model operation, reference evaluation and limitations; exact primary DOI/title/PMCID and fresh PubMed electronic date/notice metadata.
